item.title: Safeguarding and child protection
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
The welfare of children and young people is central to every Learning Net lesson, tutor decision and family conversation.

Our safeguarding commitment

The Learning Net aims to provide a safe, respectful online learning environment. Everyone working with children is expected to act in the child’s best interests, recognise concerns and report them promptly.

Designated safeguarding contact

Email: info@thelearningnet.org

If a child is in immediate danger, families should contact local emergency services or the relevant child-protection authority first.

Safer recruitment and DBS

  • Enhanced DBS checks for tutors
  • Verified identity and right to work
  • References checked before teaching
  • Ongoing training in safeguarding practice

Safe online lessons

  • Lessons use approved platforms only
  • Parents and guardians may observe sessions
  • No private messaging outside approved channels
  • Session recordings stored securely where used
  • Attendance and engagement are monitored
  • Tutors follow a clear code of conduct

Recognising and reporting concerns

All tutors are trained to recognise signs of abuse, neglect and online risk. Concerns may come from a student, a parent, another tutor or observations during a lesson.

Any concern is reported to the designated safeguarding lead without delay, and records are kept securely. Families are informed where appropriate and in line with data-protection rules.

Responding to a disclosure

  1. Listen calmly and without judgement.
  2. Reassure the child that they were right to tell you.
  3. Do not promise confidentiality; explain you must share it to keep them safe.
  4. Record what was said as soon as possible, using the child’s own words.
  5. Report to the designated safeguarding lead immediately.

Raise a safeguarding concern

Your details are sent directly to info@thelearningnet.org through The Learning Net website.

[ln_form id="safeguarding"]

Privacy and review

Safeguarding records are stored securely and retained only as required by law and child-protection practice. This policy is reviewed when guidance changes or after a safeguarding incident.

item.title: Empowering Students Through Leadership
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Published 2 March 2023

The live article carries this title and the full IGCSE revision guide below.

Understanding the IGCSE exam format

IGCSE exams are a crucial milestone. Strong preparation begins by understanding how each subject is assessed. Papers may include multiple-choice questions, structured written responses, data analysis, case studies and practical assessments.

Check the syllabus, number of papers, weighting and question types before planning revision.

Best IGCSE revision resources

Useful resources include textbooks, online courses, interactive apps and dedicated revision websites. The Learning Net supports students with IGCSE and O Level textbooks, workbooks, revision notes, video tutorials, quizzes and guided lessons.

  • Gojimo for quick subject quizzes
  • Quizlet for customisable flashcards
  • Brainscape for spaced flashcard practice

Use past papers effectively

  1. Simulate exam conditions: Complete papers under timed conditions.
  2. Review mark schemes: Study how marks are awarded.
  3. Identify weak areas: Return to topics where marks were lost.
  4. Practise regularly: Use several papers to build confidence and familiarity.

Proven study techniques

Active recall and mind maps

  • Use flashcards to retrieve key ideas
  • Create mind maps to connect related topics

Group study and discussion

Explain difficult ideas to peers; teaching someone else can expose gaps and strengthen understanding.

Exam strategy

  • Allocate time according to the marks available
  • Use relevant real-world examples where appropriate
  • Respond directly to command words such as explain, evaluate and compare

Additional support

If a topic continues to feel difficult, one-to-one tuition can provide precise explanations, guided practice and feedback.

Final thoughts

Successful IGCSE revision combines a clear plan, consistent practice and resources matched to the exact specification. Stay committed, review mistakes and build confidence one topic at a time.

item.title: The 12-week crash course: a fast track to exam confidence

A structured, focused and expert-led revision programme can bring clarity when the examination window is approaching.

Why the final 12 weeks matter

The final 12 weeks before an examination should be about clarity, confidence and precision. A focused plan brings order to the syllabus, so every study session serves a purpose.

How the crash course is structured

Each week targets specific topics, assessed through practice questions and short tests. This structure supports GCSE, IGCSE and A-Level learners, including private and homeschooling candidates.

Subjects covered

The crash course supports common subjects including English, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Biology. Ask about other subjects during enrolment.

What students gain

  • A defined weekly revision plan
  • Regular mock tests with personalised feedback
  • Targeted revision notes and exam-focused materials
  • Live 1-to-1 sessions for precise guidance
  • Flexible online access from home

A smarter route to exam day

Twelve weeks of deliberate, well-organised revision can rebuild momentum and confidence before the examination window opens.

item.title: Best way to prepare for IGCSE Maths
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Published 29 September 2023

A clear strategy builds both confidence and accuracy in IGCSE Mathematics.

1. Know your syllabus

The Edexcel and Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics syllabuses set out exactly what you must learn. Read them carefully before you begin.

2. Practise past papers

Past papers reveal the style, difficulty and timing of the real exam. Use them under timed conditions to build confidence.

3. Use revision notes

Condensed notes make recall faster. The Learning Net provides free IGCSE notes that summarise the most important points.

4. Ask for help

If a concept remains unclear, work through it with a tutor or teacher before moving on.

5. Keep going

Steady effort matters more than last-minute intensity. Review small sections regularly and track your progress.

item.title: Best way to study for IGCSEs
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Published 29 September 2023

Smart, colourful and exam-focused strategies can outperform long, unfocused study hours.

1. Understand your exam

Read the syllabus to see exactly which topics will be assessed and how the marks are allocated.

2. Create a schedule

Plan regular study blocks and balance harder topics with lighter review sessions.

3. Use colourful tools

Highlighters, colour-coded notes and diagrams make key ideas easier to remember.

4. Practise with past papers

Work through recent papers under timed conditions, then study the mark scheme to see where marks are earned.

5. Stay consistent

Short daily sessions build stronger recall than occasional long sessions. Keep notes organised and revisit weak areas.

item.title: How to tackle tricky A-Level Maths questions
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Published 19 September 2023

Tricky questions test connected understanding, not only the recall of a formula.

1. Deconstruct the question

Break each problem into smaller parts. Identify what is given, what is required and which topics are involved.

2. Make a plan

Decide the order of your working before writing. A short outline saves time and prevents errors.

3. Show your working

Clear steps earn method marks even when the final answer is wrong, so never skip the reasoning.

4. Check your answer

Substitute your answer back where possible, or estimate whether the result is reasonable.

Final thoughts

Deconstructing, planning, showing working and checking can turn an intimidating question into a sequence of manageable decisions.

item.title: 10 proven tips to boost IGCSE revision success
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Published 13 September 2023

Use these practical habits to make revision more active, consistent and manageable.

1. Start early

Begin revision well before the exam season so there is time to revisit difficult topics.

2. Set clear goals

Define what each session should achieve, such as mastering one topic or completing one past paper.

3. Use active recall

Test yourself from memory instead of re-reading notes. Flashcards and blank-page recall work well.

4. Practise past papers

Exam-style questions train timing and reveal the command words examiners use.

5. Make a timetable

Schedule subjects across the week and include short breaks to stay focused.

6. Teach someone else

Explaining a concept aloud exposes gaps in understanding.

7. Stay organised

Keep notes, papers and mark schemes in one place so revision time is not wasted searching.

8. Look after yourself

Sleep, exercise and regular meals support memory and concentration.

9. Review mistakes

Keep an error log of questions you got wrong and revisit them until they feel secure.

10. Ask for help

A tutor, teacher or study partner can explain ideas that remain unclear.

item.title: Why one-on-one learning can outperform group classes for IGCSE
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Published 24 March 2023

Focused individual attention can achieve more than larger, one-size-fits-all classes.

Personalised attention

A 1-to-1 tutor adapts the pace, examples and explanations to the individual learner.

Faster progress

Lessons target the student’s exact gaps, so less time is spent on material already understood.

Flexible scheduling

Session times can fit around school, family commitments and the learner’s energy levels.

Stronger confidence

Students ask questions freely in a private setting and receive immediate, encouraging feedback.

Final thoughts

For learners who need precise support, 1-to-1 tuition offers a focused route to stronger IGCSE results.

item.title: Ultimate guide to IGCSE revision
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Published 3 March 2023

The best IGCSE revision combines the right resources with repeated retrieval, past-paper practice and careful review.

Choosing the right resources

Match every resource to the exact specification and exam board. The Learning Net provides revision notes, video tutorials and guided lessons aligned to popular IGCSE syllabuses.

Building a revision plan

Divide the syllabus into weekly targets and schedule regular review sessions. A written plan makes progress visible and keeps momentum.

Using past papers

Complete past papers under timed conditions, then compare answers against the mark scheme to understand how marks are awarded.

Active study methods

Flashcards, mind maps and teaching a topic aloud all strengthen recall more than passive re-reading.

Staying motivated

Short goals, regular breaks and a consistent routine help revision stay manageable through the exam season.

Final thoughts

Effective preparation depends on consistency, accurate materials and honest review of mistakes. Combine revision notes with past-paper practice and seek expert help when a topic stays unclear.
